question: An ice cream store makes chocolate and vanilla ice cream by the gallon. In a week, they must make at least 5 gallons of each type but at most 10 gallons of chocolate ice cream and at most 8 gallons of vanilla ice cream. It takes 1 hour to produce a gallon of chocolate ice cream and 2 hours to produce a gallon of vanilla ice cream. In a week, 30 hours are available to make ice cream. In addition at least 6 workers are needed with 1 working on the chocolate ice cream and 2 on the vanilla ice cream at any time. If the profit per gallon of chocolate ice cream is $200 and the profit per gallon of vanilla ice cream is $300, how many gallons of each should be made to maximize profit?

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "products": ["choc", "van"],
    "profit": {"choc": 200, "van": 300},
    "lower_bound": {"choc": 5, "van": 5},
    "upper_bound": {"choc": 10, "van": 8},
    "hours_per_gallon": {"choc": 1, "van": 2},
    "hours_available": 30,
    "workers_per_gallon": {"choc": 1, "van": 2},
    "workers_min": 6,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)

    def bounds_rule(m, p):
        return (d["lower_bound"][p], d["upper_bound"][p])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=bounds_rule)

    # Objective: maximize total profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Minimum gallons per type (atomic sentence)
    def min_bound_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] >= d["lower_bound"][p]

    model.min_gallons = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=min_bound_rule)

    # Maximum gallons per type (atomic sentence)
    def max_bound_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["upper_bound"][p]

    model.max_gallons = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=max_bound_rule)

    # Total production hours available (atomic sentence)
    def hours_rule(m):
        return sum(d["hours_per_gallon"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["hours_available"]

    model.hours_limit = pyo.Constraint(rule=hours_rule)

    # At least the required number of workers must be employed (atomic sentence)
    def workers_rule(m):
        return sum(d["workers_per_gallon"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) >= d["workers_min"]

    model.workers_min = pyo.Constraint(rule=workers_rule)

    return model

#
# Constraints (numbered, with source sentence)

#   5. "at least 6 workers ... 1 on chocolate and

DATA = {
    "products": ["chocolate", "vanilla"],
    "profit": {"chocolate": 200, "vanilla": 300},
    "hours_per_gallon": {"chocolate": 1, "vanilla": 2},

    "max_gallons": {"chocolate": 10, "vanilla": 8},
    "hours_available": 30,
    "min_workers": 6,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)

    def lb_rule(m, p):
        return d["min_gallons"][p]

    def ub_rule(m, p):
        return d["max_gallons"][p]

    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.P,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda m, p: (lb_rule(m, p), ub_rule(m, p)),
    )

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    def hours_rule(m):
        return sum(d["hours_per_gallon"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["hours_available"]

    model.hours_limit = pyo.Constraint(expr=hours_rule)

    def workers_rule(m):
        return sum(d["workers_per_gallon"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) >= d["min_workers"]

    model.workers_min = pyo.Constraint(expr=workers_rule)

    return model
